newsitem.title: USA: Democrat far ahead in Wash. state governor's race.
newsitem.headline: Democrat far ahead in Wash. state governor's race.

text.p: Democrat Gary Locke holds a wide lead over his Republican opponent Ellen Craswell in Washington state's gubernatorial race, according to an opinion poll published Thursday.

Locke, the top elected official in King County, which includes Seattle, holds a 53-34 percent lead over Craswell, a former state senator, according to the poll published in the Spokane Spokesman-Review. The remaining 13 percent were undecided.

The two candidates from opposite ends of the ideological spectrum emegred from a crowded primary last month and are vying to succeed one-term Gov. Mike Lowry, a liberal Democrat who is stepping down in part because of a sexual harassment scandal.

Craswell, from the Republican Party's Christian conservative wing, is campaigning on a platform of cutting state taxes by up to one-third and sharply reducing government involvement in a wide range of areas. She has battled charges that her strong religious beliefs would cause bias in her administration.

Locke, a former state legislator in his first term as King County executive, has fought the perception that he is a liberal with a record of raising taxes. A son of Chinese immigrants, he would be the first Asian-American governor on the U.S. mainland.

The poll of 813 likely voters showed that Locke had a 50 percent favourability rating, compared with 31 percent for Craswell. About 30 percent had an unfavourable opinion of Locke, compared with 38 percent for Craswell.
The poll's margin of error was 3.5 percentage points, the newspaper said.
